A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalProfiler work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison after matching renamed experiments, renumbered appendices, and reformatted displays.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations verifying causal consistency, analyzing generated SCMs, comparing causal estimators, and measuring runtime scalability.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation results, replaces the discrete counterfactual results, and adds causal-discovery experiments in Appendix K.4.

M1.justification: The proposed generator retains its SoI-based graph and mechanism sampling, latent projection, query generation, and ground-truth estimation procedures, including Algorithms 1–11. Section 5.4 summarizes the existing pipeline. Newly documented adaptations concern evaluated baselines rather than a revised CausalProfiler algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix K.4 adds actual causal-graph discovery evaluation, extending coverage beyond causal-query estimation. The continuous and three renamed discrete SCM settings are retained. The new client-retention example in Appendix B.2.2 is configuration guidance, not an evaluated application dataset.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons among PC, GES, and DirectLiNGAM in Table 23, introducing constraint-based, score-based, and functional-model discovery methods. Existing estimator comparisons retain their participants, including DeCaFlow under hidden confounding. Updated DCM and DeCaFlow references do not constitute new comparators.

E3.justification: Compared with v2's generic random-query evaluation, v3 reports restricting discrete queries to nonzero effects with compatible complete factual observations (Appendix K.2.2). The new discovery experiment introduces SHD, F1, precision, and recall, comparing 10–20-node graphs with 1000 observations against 30–50-node graphs with 50 observations, using expected edge counts of 3N.

E4.justification: The existing test of continuous estimators on discrete SCMs is refined to examine informative, empirically instantiable counterfactual queries, replacing its earlier unrestricted failure-oriented assessment. The low-data, hidden-confounding, generated-distribution, consistency, and scalability analyses otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 Table 18 reports runtime standard deviations for the discrete experiments; that table disappears, and v3 Table 2 supplies runtime values without runtime variability. The retained experiments keep their five-seed reporting and existing statistical tests, including Benjamini–Hochberg correction.

E6.justification: Table 2 is replaced: on the renamed binary rejection space, DCM/CausalNF mean errors change from 0.0424/0.0415 to 0.1974/0.5233. CausalNF's reported 100% failure in the largest discrete space is replaced by 0%, with all six new rows reporting zero failures. These are revised-protocol results, not same-setting improvements. Table 23 adds discovery results; continuous ATE, hidden-confounding, and scalability values are retained.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1 replaces the erroneous observational specification I = empty set with sampling from the observational distribution. Appendix E corrects treatment/outcome domains from subsets of V to individual members of V. These are limited formal corrections; the coverage proposition, proof, and complexity derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a random, open-source causal benchmark generator with explicit Spaces of Interest and coverage guarantees across the three causal reasoning levels. The principal contributions and illustrative evaluation purpose remain; the new discovery evidence supports an already stated capability.

C2.justification: Despite finite-sample caveats, v2 Appendix H.2 infers that most generated SCMs are non-identifiable from sparse empirical support. v3 Appendix G.2 explicitly rejects that inference and distinguishes empirical support from population positivity and query-specific overlap. Section 4 clarifies estimation versus robustness errors, while the discrete discussion replaces failure claims with accuracy/runtime/worst-case tradeoffs. Appendix G.3 also adds qualifications about interpreting t-SNE gaps and density.

D1.justification: Appendix K.2 newly documents factual-instance matching, CausalNF dequantization/binning, DCM category decoding, Neural Spline Flows, and normalization; K.4 identifies causal-learn. Table 3 removes Markovian/semi-Markovian flag documentation. The separate statement describing a supplementary reproduction archive disappears, while the public code link remains. These disclosures do not establish when each implementation detail changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gamella et al. (2025), Reisach et al. (2021), Herdeanu et al. (2026), and Zheng et al. (2024). Related work removes specific criticisms about existing samplers' positivity reporting and graph randomness, while retaining the overall positioning. Publication updates for existing cited methods are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v3 polishes main-text prose, nests Experiments 1–2 under Section 6.3, adds a sampling summary and a second worked SoI example, and revises back matter. The standalone LLM-use and reproducibility sections disappear. The main argumentative sequence and most technical appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with substantial redistribution of tables, figures, and definition boxes. Existing ATE boxplots are reformatted and additionally displayed in main-text Figure 2, while remaining in the appendix. Three discovery tables are added, the discrete supplementary-results table is removed, and support-diagnostic captions are revised.

improvement.justification: v3 improves interpretability by correcting the empirical-support inference and defining nontrivial, empirically instantiable discrete counterfactual evaluations. The discovery experiment also substantiates a previously only-described use. The gains are limited by incomplete propagation of the positivity correction to Appendices F and G.3 and removal of discrete-runtime variability reporting. Overall, the clearer experimental specification and interpretation provide a modest net improvement.
